pairs.difference: A (chip): very high key. The off-white table fills almost the whole card and sits in the top grey level, and one near-black slab (the chip die) is dropped in the centre. The card is split into white and black with almost no middle group, so A falls outside the real range on all three of mean, contrast and gap. B (book): the teal cover is a mid-dark mass against mid-tone wood stripes, with balanced groups and no glare.
pairs.fix: Put the chip on a mid-tone coloured surface, not a white tabletop. Make the black die a soft charcoal with a lighter top face, and keep the whole board in middle tones so it does not read as black on white.

pairs.difference: A (helmet): a flat mid-grey purple backdrop. The white shell and the large dark visor give the hero a hard white-against-dark-grey split inside, but the background has no light rays or glow structure, so overall contrast is low. B (sneakers): a mid-grey wall over a near-white floor, and the dark shoe uppers stand out clearly against the floor. It is an ordinary staged product shot.
pairs.fix: Add a soft lighter radial burst or gradient behind the helmet so the backdrop has its own light and middle bands. Lift the visor from near-black to a deep amber mid-tone.

pairs.difference: A (flask): a round, lighter halo sits right behind the flask on the pink wall, a clear spotlight glow around the hero. The glass body then nearly merges with that halo in grey, so the hero separates only by green hue, not by value. B (locker): the orange locker is a mid-light block against a darker purple wall, the dark interior gives deep accents, and there is no halo.
pairs.fix: Remove the bright glowing circle behind the flask and make the pink wall one even tone. Make the liquid and glass edges darker than the wall so the flask stands out in black and white.

pairs.difference: B (UFO): the metal saucer is a mid grey on a mid-grey sky, so in grey it merges with the background and is set apart only by its white light beads and blue dome. The corners darken toward the edges, and local contrast inside the hero is soft. A (plane): a white fuselage against the blue sky, with dark engine intakes and windows that act as crisp dark accents, so the hero separates clearly by value.
pairs.fix: Make the saucer rim a much lighter polished silver with a dark underside band, so it reads clearly brighter than the sky. Keep the sky corners the same brightness as the centre.

pairs.difference: B (lunar rover): the whole top band is near-black space with stars, making a strong dark frame (vignette 0.183, above the real range). The pale rover sits on a mid-grey ground, and nearly black tyres are its only deep accents. A (bike): a mid-dark scene with dark car glass and bottom corners, and the red bike frame reads as a dark linework mass. It is dark too, but its darks belong to the scene.
pairs.fix: Lighten the sky to a soft lavender, not deep night, and keep the ground and sky close in brightness. Let the white rover be the brightest shape on a calm, mid-light ground.

pairs.difference: A (rocket): the white body is the brightest shape and the white clouds at the bottom match it, so the hero bleeds into the cloud bank. The flame merges with the white below, and the bright cloud bands along the edges keep the corners from darkening. B (balloons): mid-dark coloured balloons against a mid sky, with dark lower halves giving clear dark accents. The groups are balanced.
pairs.fix: Keep the clouds at the bottom a soft mid tone and away from the rocket's tail. Give the rocket's shadow side a clear mid-grey band so the white body separates from the clouds.

pairs.difference: A (column): a very low-key card. The plum walls go almost black and the cream column stands out as one bright mass, a strong spotlight-in-the-dark look that is darker than the real range. B (rose arch): a high-key card. Pale pink stripes and a near-white opening sit inside the arch, and the dark foliage forms a frame. Both cards fall outside the real gap range in opposite directions, so my vector gives no clear reason to pick one.

A (vault door): the wall around the door is near-white and fills the card, so the key is very light. The steel ring is a mid grey, and the orange wheel drops to a light-mid grey that barely contrasts with the inner door, so the hero is set apart by hue (orange) rather than value. There are no real dark accents. B (gate): a mid-tone sky and bricks, with the dark iron gate making strong dark linework at the centre and clear light/mid/dark groups.
pairs.fix: Turn the surrounding wall to a mid blue-grey metal, not white. Give the door ring a dark recessed shadow groove, and make the wheel a deeper burnt orange so it reads darker than the inner door.

pairs.difference: A (control panel): a white console against a mid-grey wall and counter. The hero is the brightest block, and the only darks are the small radar screen and the red button, so the dark accents are tiny. The steel counter has bright streaks. B (claw machine): a mid-tone teal room. The dark window and the dark coin slot at the bottom give strong dark accents inside the hero, and the groups read clearly.
pairs.fix: Give the console a darker front panel or deep side shadow so it has a real dark group. Calm the reflective streaks on the counter to one even mid tone.

pairs.difference: A (chess table): a mid-tone park with a light stone table and a checkerboard of dark and light squares, with shadows on the grass. B (target booth): a dark red back wall with a near-black strip along the bottom edge, and a bright white target and teddy bear on top. Its hero gap is slightly high but still stage-lit like real booth scenes. Neither card shows a clear generated tell on value.

B (satellite dish): washed out. The dish, pole and concrete are all near-white, and the sky and ground sit in the same two light grey levels. Overall contrast is very low (0.083) and the key is too high (0.8). There are no dark accents apart from a small cast shadow, and the white dish merges with the light ground. A (fan): a dark green curtain on the left and an orange wall make mid-dark groups, and the light grille and hub separate clearly.
pairs.fix: Set the dish against a deeper blue sky and a mid-tone ground. Shade the dish's inner bowl and the pole's side in a clear mid grey, and add a dark base shadow so the white rim is the only near-white.

pairs.difference: B (satellite): a bright yellow-green glow sits right behind the satellite, with burst rays that darken toward the corners: a spotlight-halo effect. The solar panels are near-black slabs and the gold foil body is a light-mid grey, so the hero's inside contrast is hard (black panels next to bright foil). A (medal box): a burst background too, but the dark red box makes a strong dark frame around a light cushion and coin, with no light halo behind it.
pairs.fix: Remove the bright glow behind the satellite and keep the burst rays an even medium green out to the corners. Lighten the solar panels to deep blue with visible cell lines, not solid black.

pattern: The generated cards give themselves away mostly through how light is placed around the hero. Many have a glow or spotlight halo right behind the hero (flask, satellite) or very bright backgrounds that swallow it: white walls, tables and clouds (vault, chip, rocket, dish). That leaves the hero set apart by hue instead of value. In black and white, the generated heroes either blur into a white-on-white key or split into hard black slabs (chip die, solar panels) and near-white, with no middle group. The real cards keep clear light, middle and dark groups, with mid-tone backgrounds and dark accents that sit inside the object.
